pr_title: Ensure that default values for platform-based flags are applied.

review_comment:
I need some walkthrough here.

As background, we expect any BuildOptions with a Starlark value set to its default won't have that entry at all in `BuildOptions.getStarlarkOptions()`. That protects against unnecessary forking of configurations that are conceptually equivalent. Does this change any of that, or is that unrelated?

I didn't realize we even had `includeDefaultValues` in `StarlarkOptionsParser` and found it was added specifically for `canonicalize-flags` at https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/33e9bf119550950ebcf0ffb2c7b372c17748dd7d. That logic, I think, wasn't meant to trigger in `bazel build`.

> Every Starlark flag has a default value defined when it is declared. If a different value is set, platform-based flags should be able to explicitly set the default and have that override the previous value, but currently they are ignored.

That makes sense. How does this code trigger that? I realize this happens in `ParsedFlagsFunction` which creates a custom `StarlarkOptionsParser` that passes that. That produces a list of flags that we need to apply to platform mapping? Then does `PlatformFlagsProducer` ensure those flags are set but *also* ensure default-set Starlark flags aren't present in the ultimate `BuildOptions` that powers the configuration?

I think I understand the bug though. The code as is doesn't even register flags being set to their defaults as something that needs to be changed, since the custom `StarlarkOptionsParser` just drops them?

This is a good point: the code at present leaves the defaults for Starlark flags in the build options.

I think what is needed is for `ParsedFlagsFunction` to indicate that some flags get set to a specific value, and that some are removed entirely. I'm not sure how to model that: possibly with an `Optional`?

> I think I understand the bug though. The code as is doesn't even register flags being set to their defaults as something that needs to be changed, since the custom StarlarkOptionsParser just drops them?

Correct, before this change, if the platform says `--//starlark:flag=default`, it just isn't present in the list of flags. So something needs to signal "this flag needs to be explicitly removed".

I'm curious what @aranguyen makes of this since I think scoped transitions will have similar issues.

Which code uses the results of `PlatformFlagsProducer` to produce the final `BuildOptions` that feed the configuration?  Is that somewhere in `BuildConfigurationKeyProducer`?
